key_insight: SQD can tolerate substantial circuit simplification, letting much of the non-Clifford and variational detail be removed from the sampling circuit with little loss in ground-state accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper quantum-chemistry workflows by reducing circuit depth and simulation cost, making near-term quantum hardware and classical pre-processing more practical.
method: Gradient-based operator pruning removes low-impact excitation operators from the VQE ansatz.
Clifford rounding snaps remaining variational parameters to the nearest Clifford angles.
Both compression steps are applied before SQD on a qubit-reduced Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Across 21 molecules, median SQD error remained within chemical accuracy at 50% compression on both pruning and rounding axes, with up to 33× simulation speedup and hardware validation on 6 molecules showing up to 2.8× transpiled-depth reduction without SQD accuracy loss.
watch_item: Compression is only safe if the sampled bitstrings still retain enough ground-state overlap, so aggressive pruning or rounding could fail for harder molecules or noisier hardware runs.
paper_title: SQD-Enabled Circuit Compression for Resource-Efficient Quantum Chemistry
